purpose: write an out-of-process minidump of one running process with MiniDumpWriteDump (the watcher calls it on a hang, with a PowerShell of the TARGET's bitness)
usage: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File dump.ps1 -ProcessId <pid> -Out <file.dmp> [-Type 0x1165]   (32-bit game: run it with C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe)
when: by hand to dump a stuck process; normally only the watcher's hang handler runs it
not_a_verb: runs on the PC under Windows PowerShell 5.1, outside the repo checkout

purpose: install or uninstall the watcher on the PC from a harness kit: sha256-checked copy into the watcher root, a logon scheduled task (Register-ScheduledTask, no admin), first start and a health check
usage: "Install watcher.cmd" / "Uninstall watcher.cmd" (double-click); or powershell -File install.ps1 -Kit <kit dir> [-Root <dir>] [-Uninstall] [-NoTask] [-NoStart] [-TaskName <name>]
when: once per PC for the first install (Liam); host tests run it with -NoTask or a test task name; later updates use the watcher's update job, not this
not_a_verb: runs on the PC under Windows PowerShell 5.1 from the kit folder, outside the repo checkout

purpose: double-click installer for the watcher: copies the kit's harness files into the watcher root (sha256 checked) and registers the logon task "napoleon_remastered watcher" (no admin rights)
usage: double-click it in the harness kit folder (Liam, once per PC); undo with "Uninstall watcher.cmd" from the same kit; options for the PowerShell script: install.ps1 -Root <dir> -NoTask -NoStart
when: first install of the watcher on a PC; later updates go through the watcher's update job (no double-click)
not_a_verb: a Windows double-click wrapper around install.ps1

purpose: agent helper for the device VM: submit a watcher job, block inside ONE call until its result (or a timeout), print the output, return the job's exit code (refused 2, no answer 124); also take, refresh and release the game lock
usage: job.sh [--adapter FILE] <owner> <file|-> [timeout_s]  |  job.sh [--adapter FILE] lock <owner> <session> <purpose> [hang_s]  |  touch  |  unlock <owner> [--force]  |  status  |  root
when: every time an agent runs something on the PC (launch, kill, profile, scripts): the watcher root comes from the adapter (device_mount + watcher_subdir), never a default path; waiting belongs here, not in repeated agent calls
not_a_verb: runs in the device VM's bash (python3 and the PC's folders mounted), outside the repo checkout

purpose: suspend or resume every thread of a process (NtSuspendProcess / NtResumeProcess): the way to force a hang for the watchdog test, without killing anything
usage: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File procfreeze.ps1 -ProcessId <pid> -Mode suspend|resume   (as a ps1 job: "#job type=ps1 owner=<lock owner>" then & "<root>\src\procfreeze.ps1" ...)
when: PC test of the hang watchdog (suspend the game, expect a minidump, an archive under runs\ and a kill); resume to undo a test that was not meant to hang
not_a_verb: runs on the PC under Windows PowerShell 5.1, outside the repo checkout

purpose: start a program fully detached from the calling job (WMI Win32_Process.Create), so it inherits none of the job's handles and is not in its process tree
usage: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File spawn_detached.ps1 -Path <x.cmd|x.exe> [-Arguments "<args>"] [-Cwd <dir>] [-Visible]   (from a watcher job; the job must print a line)
when: any long-lived process a job starts (a probe, a test watcher, the updater); never with cmd's `start` inside a job
not_a_verb: runs on the PC under Windows PowerShell 5.1, outside the repo checkout

purpose: double-click uninstaller for the watcher: stops it, removes the logon task and moves the installed harness files to _to_delete (jobs, logs and runs are kept)
usage: double-click it in the harness kit folder; the PowerShell script is install.ps1 -Uninstall
when: when the watcher should leave the PC; nothing in the game folder is touched
not_a_verb: a Windows double-click wrapper around install.ps1

purpose: in-place update of the live watcher from a harness kit with a dead-man switch: the new watcher must come up, answer a noop job and stay alive, or the old files are put back byte for byte
usage: started detached by the watcher's "update kit=<kit id>" job (a copy of this file runs, because the update replaces src\update.ps1); by hand: powershell -File update.ps1 -Root <watcher root> -Kit <kit dir> [-NoopS 60] [-HealthyS 90] [-StableS 30]
when: whenever harness files change on the PC after the first install (never copy them by hand); the first install is "Install watcher.cmd
not_a_verb: runs on the PC under Windows PowerShell 5.1, outside the repo checkout

purpose: PROBE ONLY: list the displays and the virtual display driver's modes, and test whether it accepts given resolutions with CDS_TEST; changes nothing and prints the vdd_settings.xml edit when a mode is missing
usage: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File vdisplay_probe.ps1 [-Test 1920x1080,2560x1440] [-Hz 60] [-Name "Virtual Display Driver"]   (as a watcher ps1 job; exit 0 = all tested modes accepted, 3 = no unique virtual display, 6 = a mode is not offered)
when: before headless work needs a resolution other than the driver's current one (Empire's driver offered only 3840x2160 and refused 1080p and 1440p with DISP_CHANGE_BADMODE)
not_a_verb: runs on the PC under Windows PowerShell 5.1, outside the repo checkout

purpose: launcher loop for the watcher: restarts watcher.ps1 after a crash or a restart request, stops when told to or when another watcher owns the root
usage: started at logon by the scheduled task "napoleon_remastered watcher" (Install watcher.cmd); by hand: double-click it. Optional arguments are passed on (-Root <dir> -Adapter <file>)
when: never edit it while it runs (cmd re-reads batch files from disk): edit watcher.ps1 and send an update or restart job instead
not_a_verb: a Windows batch launcher that runs on the PC

purpose: the PC watcher: runs job requests dropped into <root>\jobs\ by cloud agents (control jobs launch/kill/profile/status/noop/restart/update, cmd and ps1 scripts) one at a time, enforces the game lock, watches the game for hangs, restores config profiles byte for byte
usage: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File watcher.ps1 [-Root <dir>] [-Adapter <adapter.json>]   (started by watch.cmd; protocol, layout and settings: harness/README.md)
when: runs permanently on the PC after "Install watcher.cmd"; agents never start it, they submit jobs with harness/core/job.sh
not_a_verb: a Windows PowerShell 5.1 service loop that runs on the PC, not a repo operation

purpose: run the harness host test suites (unit, integration or all) under the PowerShell that launches it and exit non-zero on any failure
usage: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Run-HostTests.ps1 [-Suite unit|integration|all] [-Repo <repo root>]
when: CI job harness-windows runs it with -Suite all under Windows PowerShell 5.1; locally -Suite unit works under pwsh on Linux
not_a_verb: a PowerShell test runner, not a repo operation

purpose: integration host tests for the harness on Windows: a real watcher (through watch.cmd) with fake games, driven by job files; refusals, lock, launch/kill, zombie, profiles, auto-restore, hang dump and archive, timeouts, queue rules, update with rollback, installer and uninstaller
usage: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Test-Integration.ps1 [-Repo <repo root>]   (CI: GitHub's Windows runner, Windows PowerShell 5.1; needs python for the real-kit test)
when: on every push (CI job harness-windows); never on the PC, it starts and kills processes named Fake*.exe and sets the time zone of the machine while it runs
not_a_verb: a PowerShell test script, not a repo operation

purpose: tiny shared test kit for the harness host tests (Test-Case, assertions, Wait-Until, temp folders, a test adapter); dot-sourced by Test-Unit.ps1 and Test-Integration.ps1
usage: . "$PSScriptRoot\Test-Lib.ps1"   (not run on its own)
when: only from the harness host tests; ASCII only, no Pester (Windows PowerShell 5.1 ships Pester 3 and the runner another)
not_a_verb: a dot-sourced PowerShell library for the host tests

purpose: static and unit host tests for the harness: every learning from Empire's watcher history as a guard (BOM-less UTF-8, byte[] returns, UTC everywhere, id and lock rules, hang verdicts, overlays, profile snapshot/restore, tolerant status reads)
usage: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Test-Unit.ps1 [-Repo <repo root>]   (CI: Windows PowerShell 5.1; the pure parts also run under pwsh on Linux)
when: on every push (CI job harness-windows) and before committing a change to harness/
not_a_verb: a PowerShell test script, not a repo operation

purpose: build the proxy d3d9.dll (mingw-w64 i686, the release route) and/or build and run the host tests (g++)
usage: proxy/tools/build.sh [dll|tests|all|smoke|repro] [--adapter napoleon]   (smoke: run the built DLL under wine with a stand-in exe; repro: rebuild from a copy at another path, fail unless byte-identical)   (outputs in build/proxy/; needs g++-mingw-w64-i686 for dll)
when: after any change under proxy/ (CI runs `all` on every push); the DLL in build/proxy/<adapter>/d3d9.dll is what proxy/tools/pc_deploy.py kits
not_a_verb: a compiler driver for C++ sources, not a registry operation; CI and agents call it directly

purpose: print an exe's identity (sha1, PE TimeDateStamp, SizeOfImage, CheckSum, LAA/ASLR/NX flags, sections, DRM stub signs) and its d3d9.dll imports, and check that the proxy's d3d9.def exports cover them
usage: python3 proxy/tools/exe_info.py <Napoleon.exe> [--def proxy/core/d3d9.def] [--identity proxy/napoleon/identity.json]
when: to re-check the target exe before pinning it or after a Steam update (runs on the PC's device VM against the game folder, or anywhere on a copy); exit 1 when the identity file or the def file disagrees
not_a_verb: it must run on the PC's device VM, which has the game folder but no repo checkout with the core submodule; copy this one file there

purpose: download the pinned stock DXVK release tarball, verify its sha256, extract x32/d3d9.dll as d3d9_dxvk.dll plus DXVK's LICENSE, and verify both
usage: python3 proxy/tools/fetch_dxvk.py [--out build/dxvk] [--print-pin]
when: before kitting the proxy for the PC (pc_deploy.py kit runs it); to move to a newer DXVK change PIN below (version, URLs, three sha256) in its own commit
not_a_verb: needs network and writes build output, not a registry operation; pc_deploy.py and agents call it directly

purpose: turn registries/engine_sites.jsonl, registries/config_keys.jsonl and proxy/<game>/identity.json into proxy/<game>/generated/tables.h and the shipped default config file, validating every site (hex, lengths, overlaps, config key, exe pin)
usage: python3 proxy/tools/gen_tables.py [--adapter proxy/napoleon] [--check]
when: after any change to the engine_sites or config_keys registry or identity.json (then rebuild the DLL); --check runs in the gates (tests/test_proxy_tables.py) and fails when the generated files are stale or a site is invalid
not_a_verb: games cannot add wsc verbs for the proxy yet (wsc.toml verb_dirs is empty and the generator moves to warscape-core with proxy/core at the end of phase 1); the gates reach it through tests/

purpose: build a proxy kit (built DLL, default config, pinned DXVK) or a harness kit (the watcher, its adapter and profiles; manifest with sha256 and unique staged names), install the proxy into the game folder with sha-checked copies, uninstall it back to the pre-install snapshot, edit the installed config, snapshot and diff a game folder
usage: pc_deploy.py kit [--what proxy|harness] [--out DIR] | snapshot --game G --out F | install --kit DIR --game G --state S [--assume-closed] | uninstall --game G --state S [--assume-closed] | set --game G key=value... | status --game G --state S | diff A B
when: every time built proxy or harness files go to the PC or come off it (never copy them by hand); `kit` in the cloud, the rest on the PC's device VM (python3, the game folder mounted) or on Windows; install/uninstall ask the running watcher (<state>/watcher/watcher.status) whether a game of either title is running
not_a_verb: it runs on the PC's device VM, which has no repo checkout or core submodule (copy this one file there with the kit); stdlib only

purpose: turn WER LocalDumps for Napoleon.exe off again (removes only its own registry subkey); asks for admin rights once
usage: double-click it
when: when crash dumps are no longer wanted
not_a_verb: a Windows double-click wrapper around wer_localdumps.ps1

purpose: turn on WER LocalDumps (full crash dumps, out of process) for Napoleon.exe only; asks for admin rights once
usage: double-click it (Liam, once per PC); undo with "Disable crash dumps.cmd
when: before the first PC test of the proxy; the dumps go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps\napoleon_remastered
not_a_verb: a Windows double-click wrapper around wer_localdumps.ps1

purpose: turn Windows Error Reporting LocalDumps on, off or report it for ONE exe (default Napoleon.exe): full dumps written out of process, so they work when the game's heap is corrupt and the in-process minidump is empty
usage: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File wer_localdumps.ps1 -Mode status|enable|disable [-ExeName Napoleon.exe] [-DumpFolder <path>] [-DumpCount 5]   (enable/disable need an elevated prompt: "Enable crash dumps.cmd")
when: once per PC before PC tests (Liam runs "Enable crash dumps.cmd"); after any start-up crash read these dumps FIRST (empire-remastered LEARNINGS lesson 23)
not_a_verb: runs on Windows as administrator, outside the repo checkout

purpose: Refuse a pull request whose branch is not a reviewed job, a brief, a planning change or a repo-infrastructure change.
usage: python3 tools/pr_policy.py --branch <head branch> [--base origin/main]   (CI runs it on every pull request)
when: automatic in CI (`policy` job); locally before opening a pull request to see what CI will say.
not_a_verb: it reads pull-request metadata that only CI has; it becomes a core gate once warscape-core supports game gates (backlog B1).
